articles.headline: Chiefs roll into Week 6 unbeaten as winless Chargers face a daunting trip to Kansas City
articles.description: — The Kansas City Chiefs are the last remaining unbeaten team in the AFC, and one of just three in the entire NFL heading into Week 6, while the Los Angeles Chargers are among the suffering trio of teams that have yet to win a game.
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- — The Kansas City Chiefs are the last remaining unbeaten team in the AFC, and one of just three in the entire NFL heading into Week 6, while the Los Angeles Chargers are among the suffering trio of teams that have yet to win a game.


              In many ways, it's back to normal for the Chiefs after a down season by their standards. But it's wholly unusual for the Chargers, who are coming off back-to-back 11-win seasons under Jim Harbaugh but are off to their worst start in more than two decades.


              “One of the things we were all put on this Earth to do was to handle both success and loss," Harbaugh said recently, “to do that with the same passion and enthusiasm and to show that you belong.”


              Yet it's hard to fathom the Chargers having a whole lot of passion when they head to Kansas City on Sunday.


              Not only are the Chiefs among the league's highest-scoring teams again, and their defense under coordinator Steve Spagnuolo once again holding teams in check, they are coming off a bye — and Andy Reid is almost unbeatable in those situations. 


              Teams going back to his days with the Philadelphia Eagles are a combined 22-5 during the regular season when given a week off.


              “We know that records don't matter. They've been in every game and they're playing their tail off,” Reid said of the Chargers, pointing out that much of the roster is the same from the bunch that beat Kansas City twice last season.


              The second matchup in December was the game in which Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes tore ligaments in his left knee.


              Mahomes is back to playing at a high level, though, helped by the success of free-agent acquisition Kenneth Walker III in the Chiefs' backfield. They're hitting deep passes as they were during Mahomes' early days in the league, and the fact he's been able to scramble, create and run the Kansas City offense without his knee causing any issues has put everyone in their building at ease.


              His counterpart, Justin Herbert, has been a microcosm — or a big reason for — many of the Chargers' problems. He's tied with Patriots quarterback Drake Maye for the most interceptions in the league, and only the Browns' Deshaun Watson has been sacked more entering Week 6.


              “Listen, it’s a divisional opponent, so those games are really, really, really important,” Chiefs pass rusher George Karlaftis said. “With them not having gotten any wins, they’re going to be hungry. They’re going to be hungry to get their first win, and they’d like nothing more than to get a win against us. So, we’ve got to be on our stuff. It’s a team that their record, I don’t think, is indicative of the team that they are. They’re in every game, and we have a lot of respect for them.”


              Need to know
              Los Angeles Chargers (0-5) at Kansas City (4-0)


              When/where to watch: Sunday,

articles.headline: Jameis Winston’s starting dream is alive as the Giants roll into a game against the Saints
articles.description: — When Jameis Winston signed with the New Orleans Saints in 2020 initially to back up Drew Brees and then to be in the mix to succeed him at quarterback, he was long removed from winning the Heisman...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- — When Jameis Winston signed with the New Orleans Saints in 2020 initially to back up Drew Brees and then to be in the mix to succeed him at quarterback, he was long removed from winning the Heisman Trophy in college and being the top pick in the draft.


              He did not give up on being a starter in the NFL again, like he was early in his career with Tampa Bay.


              “I dreamt of it,” Winston said Wednesday. “And now it's here.”


              Winston got another chance with the New York Giants this season after Jaxson Dart was lost for the season with a knee injury. He's still unbeaten since assuming the full-time No. 1 role, and while J.J. McCarthy is getting mixed in as a change of pace, this is firmly Winston's job with New Orleans up next Sunday.


              “He’s a leader," said Saints defensive end Carl Granderson, who was teammates with Winston for four seasons. "He’s going to bring the energy. He’s going to make sure the offense is ready to play. He’s the hype man of their team, so we’ve just got to be ready to get after them and have even more energy than he’s bringing.”


              Energy isn't the issue. Efficiency is, and Winston has been all over the map since stepping in for Dart.


              In relief at the Los Angeles Rams — New York's only loss — Winston was 11 of 27 with an interception. He managed an ugly victory against Tennessee, provided the full so-called “Jameis Winston experience” to beat Arizona and improved drastically along the way at Washington, a game that ended in an infamous tie.


              "It’s tough to just kind of jump in there when the offense is built probably for a different quarterback," coach John Harbaugh said. “It was awkward, and he fought through it and he kept his confidence. He kept his poise, and he found a way to win football games. Now we’re starting to get adapted, I think, a little bit to the game plan and what we’re doing and getting reps on the things that are more Jameis-type things.”


              While the Giants are 3-1-1 and alone in first place in the NFC East, the Saints are 1-4 after losing three in a row. Their lone victory came on the road, when Tyler Shough was 27 of 34 for 252 yards and two touchdowns — one each passing and rushing — at Baltimore.


              That TD was one of 39 successful completions between Shough and receiver Chris Olave this season.


              “Those two guys, they’re a connection right now,” Harbaugh said. “He’s been lighting it up since he started. But he’s still a young quarterback too, so you see all those elements. Done a great job, though.”


              Need to know
              New Orleans (1-4) at N.Y. Giants (3-1-1)


              When/where to watch: Sunday 1 p.m. EDT, Fox.


              Latest odds: Saints by 1 1/2.


              Against the spread: Saints 2-3; Giants 4-1.

articles.headline: Patriots star WR A.J. Brown says status 'still up in the air' for game vs. Jets
articles.description: Patriots WR A.J. Brown said his status for Sunday's game against the Jets is "still up in the air" after returning to practice this week.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown said his status for Sunday's game against the New York Jets is "still up in the air" after returning to practice this week for the first time since suffering a right high-ankle sprain in the season opener.

"I felt pretty good," Brown said while noting he was taking a "one step at a time" approach, which included seeing how the ankle responded Thursday in a practice with full shoulder pads that promised to be more physical.

"Obviously it's going to be a Coach Vrabel decision, to see where I'm at and make the better decision for the long haul, not just for temporarily," he said.

The Patriots (3-2) have a quick turnaround after Sunday's game against the Jets (2-3), traveling to face the Chicago Bears on Thursday, Oct. 22.

Brown was a limited participant in practice Wednesday. He said his goal is to add to his workload on a daily basis.

"It felt good just to be back on the grass practicing. Working on the side is a little boring," he said.

Brown shared a personal story of his reaction to the injury, which occurred in the third quarter of New England's season-opening loss to the Seahawks in Seattle. As he lay on the field, he said he was thinking about how he would not be able to attend his wife Kelsey's graduation from nursing school that weekend in New Jersey.

Brown said he appreciated coach Mike Vrabel excusing him from mandatory rehabilitation to attend.

articles.headline: Man United's Martínez issues apology for post-match outburst after meeting
articles.description: Lisandro Martínez has issued a formal apology after criticising Manchester United's board following the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.
articles.body:
Lisandro Martínez has issued a formal apology after criticising Manchester United's board following Tuesday's 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.

The Argentina defender took aim at director of football Jason Wilcox during his post-match interviews and suggested head coach Michael Carrick has been let down by a lack of summer signings.

United's hierarchy, including Wilcox and Carrick, met with Martínez  at the club's training ground on Thursday before the 28-year-old released a statement apologising for his comments.

"Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager," Martínez said in a post on social media.

"It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

"Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

"The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise."

United have chosen not to confirm whether Martínez has been disciplined for his outburst, although sources have told ESPN that he has been fined.

According to club sources, the matter is "considered closed" and Martínez is set to be available to face Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday if selected.

articles.headline: Backup plan guide: Seven late-round picks one break away from fantasy success
articles.description: Jim McCormick points out which late-round picks could be close to fantasy basketball stardom.
articles.body:
Midway through the 2011-2012 season, on the heels of losing 11 of 13 games, New York Knicks coach Mike D'Antoni had seemingly no options left in his backcourt. Baron Davis was absent due to a bad back, while Iman Shumpert was sidelined with a knee ailment. The coach turned to a combo guard -- averaging 3.6 points in 6.1 minutes -- to save the season.

Within days, the sports world, and fantasy leagues, were immersed in Linsanity. The actionable lesson in Jeremy Lin's sudden ascent is that we should appreciate how fragile rosters and thin depth charts can produce magical fantasy basketball outcomes. Predicting Lin would become a star wasn't easy. Expecting someone to step up in a valuable D'Antoni offense was. Lin might never have seen the court that winter had he been part of a stable, healthy, and bankable backcourt.

Ryan Rollins was, albeit with far less hype, last season's Lin: a gifted, overlooked combo guard who scaled a thin backcourt depth chart to become a fantasy star. The Milwaukee Bucks entered last season without trusted scoring or shot creation past Giannis Antetokounmpo. While it was surely surprising that Rollins, a player undrafted in most leagues, ended up No. 30 overall on the Player Rater, the context of his team's roster invited a leap.

The focus of this piece is to consider which players around the league might have a far higher ceiling than the market currently appreciates. Sometimes, a player is a trade, injury or promotion away from an enduring and rewarding role.

A single Shams Charania post can change multiple depth charts in an instant. Consider this the contingency tier of talents: those who require some blend of luck, development, timing and trust in order to pop. What widely available players, sitting in free agency in your league or found in the twilight rounds of all drafts ahead of the 2026-27 season, can become the statistical forces that Lin, Rollins, and many others have been in seasons past?

It's likely Mitchell would inherit a major role if either of SGA or Jalen Williams were sidelined.

articles.headlineJa: NFL第6週のユニフォーム：ブロンコスとシーホークスがTNFの対戦で復刻モデルを着用
articles.descriptionJa: ブロンコスとシーホークスの復刻モデル着用を中心に、NFL各チームの第6週のユニフォームを紹介する。
articles.body:
Throwback Thursday is coming to the NFL in Week 6 with a matchup for nostalgic eyes on "Thursday Night Football." The Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks will each wear their throwback uniforms in the game.

Denver's look is a callback to the 1977 uniforms that honor the "Orange Crush" era. The orange jerseys include oversized white numbers in legacy blue trim, while white pants and legacy blue helmet complete the look. Featured on the lid is the iconic hissing Bronco and "D" on the side. The Broncos boast a 5-0 record since debuting the combination in the 2024 campaign.

Seattle is throwing it back to the 1990s with its royal blue jerseys, and matching silver helmet and pants. Running on the uniform's sleeve is a classic Seahawks logo on top of green and blue stripes. Neatly, the old Kingdome appears on the inside collar. The matte silver helmet is similar to what the franchise wore in its early history. The Seahawks have a 4-3 record in the throwbacks since debuting them in 2023. 

The alternate uniform space is well represented, too, as the New Orleans Saints are wearing their all-white color rush uniforms with a white helmet against the New York Giants. New Orleans unveiled the white lids in 2025 with a new tri-color stripe down the center and a black face mask for the first time in franchise history. A mini fleur-de-lis is subtly included on the tri-color stripe.

articles.headline: Victor Wembanyama, Spurs dominate annual NBA GM survey
articles.description: An annual survey of NBA GMs projects the Spurs to win the NBA title this season, with Victor Wembanyama earning MVP and Defensive Player of the Year honors.
articles.body:
An annual survey of NBA general managers revealed Thursday that the league is bracing for a full takeover by Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs.

After winning 62 games and making a surprise trip to the NBA Finals last season, the Spurs emerged as the survey's 2027 championship favorite, and Wembanyama was projected to win Most Valuable Player and be selected as the league's best defensive player.

In addition, the 7-foot-4 French center received 93% of the votes in response to the question: "If you were starting a franchise today and could sign any player in the NBA, who would it be?"

The general managers did not view the Spurs as overwhelming title favorites. San Antonio received 50% of the votes, narrowly topping the 2025 champion Oklahoma City Thunder. The defending champion New York Knicks, who were picked to win the Eastern Conference, and the new-look Philadelphia 76ers, bolstered by LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, also received votes to win the title.

Wembanyama, 22, was selected as the heavy favorite to win his first MVP award with 77% of the votes. Denver's Nikola Jokic (10%) and Minnesota's Anthony Edwards (7%) also earned nods.

While Wembanyama was also selected as the "player who forces opposing coaches to make the most adjustments," the "best international player" and "the most versatile player," he wasn't the only Spurs star to receive recognition in the extensive survey.

Dylan Harper, the 2025 No. 2 pick, was voted as the player most likely to enjoy a breakthrough season, topping Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg. Tobias Harris, a veteran forward who signed with San Antonio in free agency, was also named as the offseason's "most underrated player acquisition." Finally, the Spurs' young core, which includes Wembanyama, Harper and Stephon Castle, was named as the league's most promising.

The league's general managers deemed the 76ers as winners of the "best overall moves this offseason" for adding James and Brown, topping the Miami Heat and Charlotte Hornets. However, Miami's trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo was viewed as the "acquisition who will make the biggest impact."

NBA.com has conducted a survey of the league's general managers for the past 25 seasons. This year's edition featured 48 questions regarding players, teams and recent transactions.

articles.headline: Las Vegas bettor Shane Hennen pleads guilty to charges related to fixing schemes
articles.description: A bettor indicted in three federal gambling cases pleaded guilty to charges related to schemes involving the NBA, NCAA and Chinese Basketball Association.
articles.body:
Shane Hennen, a Las Vegas sports bettor indicted in three high-profile federal gambling cases, pleaded guilty to charges related to betting schemes involving the NBA, the NCAA and the Chinese Basketball Association on Wednesday in Philadelphia.

Hennen pleaded guilty to sports bribery, aiding and abetting and conspiracy charges related to wire fraud and money laundering in two of the cases in federal court.

The maximum sentence is 125 years in prison, according to the Department of Justice's plea memorandum. His sentencing is scheduled for Feb. 25, 2027.

Federal prosecutors from the U.S. Attorney's Office in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania say Hennen participated in a nearly three-year scheme that began around September 2022 and aimed to fix basketball games in the Chinese Basketball Association CBA and in NCAA basketball.

"The defendant engaged in the scheme as a 'fixer,' working together with others who recruited and bribed CBA and NCAA men's basketball players to underperform and help ensure their team failed to cover the spread," federal prosecutors stated in the court documents. "The defendant then placed large wagers on those games, and arranged for others to do so, generating proceeds for the scheme."

Hennen also pleaded guilty to participating in a scheme to use nonpublic information to bet on NBA games and players in a case from the Eastern District of New York involving Terry Rozier.

An attorney for Hennen declined comment when reached Thursday by ESPN.

Hennen is still facing charges in a third case involving allegedly rigged poker games backed by the Mafia. NBA coach and Hall of Famer Chauncey Billups and former NBA player and coach Damon Jones were also indicted in the poker case.

It is the way of the soccer world right now that competitions must get larger, with more teams, more matches per team and a much lower average reading on the jeopardy per match scale.

Aside from the obvious wear-and-tear concerns, I don't really mind this development. (Maybe it's the American in me: I'm used to bloat.)

I don't mind that the Euros have 24 teams, or that the Champions League has 36, or that the World Cup has 48 -- and that two-thirds of the competitors reach the knockout rounds in all of these tournaments. That has allowed for super-cool stories to develop.

Ukraine snuck into the knockout rounds at Euro 2020 (amid growing geopolitical stress) and then upset Sweden. Slovenia and Slovakia eked out advancement in 2024, too, and nearly pulled upsets. And while a huge Champions League with a huge set of knockout rounds has allowed more time for struggling powers like PSG and Manchester City in 2024-25 to rebound from poor starts, it also allowed Bodø/Glimt to find their footing and eventually take down Manchester City, Atlético Madrid and Inter Milan, consecutively, while nearly making the quarterfinals last season.

I don't mind bloat as long as it allows for proper storytelling and extra world-building. In a world with tilted finances, where only a few teams are actually capable of winning the whole thing, a fun journey almost matters more than the eventual destination.

Matchday 1 of this year's Champions League concerned me a bit in that regard. There was still fun to be had -- Como ran away from RB Leipzig in their first ever European group stage game, Real Madrid outlasted Inter Milan in a battle of European royalty, and 11 of 18 matches featured at least four goals. Goals are fun.

- UCL Talking Points: Who's to blame for Man United mess?

- Reaction: Man City can't compete with gold standard PSG

- Kirkland: Real Madrid did win, but glory feels far away

Still, Davids weren't exactly scoring damage points on Goliaths. PSG, Barcelona and Bayern Munich beat Slovan Bratislava, Feyenoord and Bodø/Glimt by a combined 16-2, and debutants LASK, Sabah and Viking all lost by a combined 8-1. It was a foreboding start, a sign that maybe Europe's giants have even further distanced themselves from the pack. I'm a fan of storytelling, and that's the least fun story to tell.

Luckily, Matchday 2 gave us delightful plot twists and track meets.

It also took us to Norway.

Main characters of the week

No. 1: Viking FK

Viking FK has lived a full club life since its founding in Stavanger in 1899: Early regional titles in the 1920s and 1930s; national titles in the 1950s, when that became a thing to aspire to; great spells (four straight titles in the 1970s); poor spells (relegation in 1986 and 2017); the requisite financial overextension in the 2010s (who among us).

On occasion, they've also enjoyed the glory of home European nights. They hosted Borussia Mönchengladbach (and drew 1-1) in the 1979-80 UEFA Cup, held Barcelona to a 0-0 draw in q

articles.headline: Tyler, The Creator joins stars to appear on Barcelona Clásico kit
articles.description: It's become a tradition in recent years for Barcelona to add the logo of top music stars to their jerseys when they face Real Madrid in El Clásico.
articles.headlineJa: タイラー・ザ・クリエイター、バルセロナのクラシコ用キットに登場するスター陣に加わる
articles.descriptionJa: 近年、バルセロナはエル・クラシコでレアル・マドリードと対戦する際、トップミュージシャンのロゴをユニフォームに加えることを恒例としている。
articles.body:
It's become something of a tradition in recent years for Barcelona to change up their kits when they face Real Madrid in El Clásico.

As part of their massive sponsorship deal with Spotify, Barça have been sporting the trademark logos of some of the biggest music acts when they face their bitter rivals in LaLiga matches. This began in 2022, when Drake became the first international star to have his own emblem replace the standard Spotify logo on the front of the Catalan club's jersey.

With the first Clásico of the 2026-27 season almost upon us, Barça have revealed the identity of the latest big-named act who will be gracing their jerseys for the fixture with the honor going to eclectic rapper and fashionista Tyler, The Creator.

The multiple Grammy-winning hip-hop star therefore becomes the ninth musical act to have its logo worn by Barça during El Clásico in the space of the past five years. He joins an exclusive club of acts to be given the honor, including Coldplay, Ed Sheeran and Olivia Rodrigo -- all of whom have seen their custom marques added to special-edition kits in lieu of a traditional front-of-shirt sponsor.

- Watch El Clasico, Oct. 25 at 3 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN+ (U.S.)

- Liverpool fans 'welcome' City in first match since guilty verdict

2022-23

DRAKE, Oct. 16, 2022 (Real Madrid 3-1 Barcelona)

Less than a year into Barça's ongoing deal with Spotify, with the club's Camp Nou stadium also bearing the name of the streaming giant, Drake became the first musician to have his logo adorn the hallowed red-and-blue striped jersey when the Canadian rapper's "OVO" owl label was on display during a disappointing defeat at the Bernabéu in the first Clásico of the season.

ROSALÍA, March 19, 2023 (Barcelona 2-1 Real Madrid)

Catalonia-born pop star Rosalía proved to be a much brighter omen for Barça, who won the reverse fixture at Camp Nou while wearing the logo for her "Motomami" album across their shirts.

2023-24

THE ROLLING STONES, Oct. 28, 2023 (Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid)

The Stones marked the release of their first album in 18 years, "Hackney Diamonds," by slapping their iconic lips and tongue logo to the Barcelona shirt. Lamine Yamal made his Clásico debut (played at the city's Olympic stadium as renovations at Camp Nou began) but unfortunately the home side fell to defeat via two second-half goals from Jude Bellingham.

KAROL G, April 21, 2024 (Real Madrid 3-2 Barcelona)

Barça narrowly lost out to another late Bellingham strike, this time at the Bernabéu, while wearing bespoke shirts with the signature barbed-wire heart logo of Colombian singer and songwriter Karol G on the front.

2024-25

COLDPLAY, Oct. 26, 2024 (Real Madrid 0-4 Barcelona)

articles.headline: Marc Guéhi hails Man City unity amid financial charges fallout
articles.description: Marc Guéhi hailed Manchester City's unity in the face of adversity after a spirited fightback in the club's first home match since being found guilty of multiple breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.
articles.headlineJa: マーク・グエイ、財務規則違反の処分に直面する中でのマン・シティの結束を称賛
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグの財務規則に対する複数の違反で有罪判決を受けた後、クラブにとって初のホームゲームで力強い反撃を見せたことを受け、マーク・グエイは逆境におけるマンチェスター・シティの結束を称賛した。
articles.body:
Marc Guéhi hailed Manchester City's unity in the face of adversity after a spirited fightback in the club's first home match since being found guilty of multiple breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

City were beaten 4-2 by Paris St Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday but only after a rousing response to being swatted aside 3-0 by the holders in the first half at the Etihad Stadium.

It was a night when City showed their defiance in the face of the last month's damning verdict by an independent commission, which found the club had broken Premier League rules.

Former manager Pep Guardiola was in attendance in a strong show of support for the under-fire hierarchy, who have appealed against the judgement, while fans unveiled a huge "City Til I Die" tifo to make underline their loyalty.

A ferocious atmosphere threatened to fall flat as PSG produced a clinical first-half display but it was reenergised after the break as City produced enough chances -- including hitting the woodwork twice - to threaten an unlikely comeback.

Defender Guehi said: "I think the support that we've had from the fans and the football club has been fantastic and everyone's definitely together in this.

"I think it says a lot about, not just the players, but the football club in general. It's very easy when adversity comes to focus on that, but everyone's been focused on what's in front of them, which is the games.

"As long as we carry on playing like we did in the second half and training well, things will look positive for us."

City were ripped apart by the back-to-back champions in the first half, with quickfire goals from Désiré Doué and Ousmane Dembélé establishing control.

- Man City can't compete with PSG, the Champions League's gold standard

- Man City's Antoine Semenyo on missed chances against PSG: 'Beating myself up'

The game seemed all but over when Vitinha made it 3-0 with 32 minutes gone but a triple substitution by Enzo Maresca at the break sparked a chaotic second period.

Erling Haaland struck twice -- becoming City's record Champions League goalscorer in the process with 38 from 41 appearances -- while also hitting the crossbar and seeing Enzo Fernández denied by the post.

But the task was to prove just beyond City as PSG claimed a fourth when a Maghnes Akliouche effort squeezed past a despairing Gianluigi Donnarumma. Former City striker Ferran Torres also missed a late penalty for the visitors.

Guehi said: "Playing at home, it's not really acceptable, that performance in the first half, in front of our home fans, so I'm just really glad everyone reacted in a positive manner and at least came out fighting.

"For the first goals, they were just a bit more aggressive, won a lot of the 1v1 duels, which allowed them the platform to go score those goals.

"But the second half was the complete opposite. We were a lot more aggressive, won a lot more of the duels, which gave us the platform.

articles.headline: Dembélé jokes he might ask for more holidays after PSG's win at Man City
articles.description: Ousmane Dembélé joked he might ask coach Luis Enrique for more time off after starring in PSG's 4-2 win at Manchester City in the Champions League.
articles.body:
Ousmane Dembélé joked he might ask coach Luis Enrique for more time off after starring in Paris Saint-Germain's 4-2 win at Manchester City in the Champions League.

The Ballon d'Or winner scored one goal and assisted on another in Wednesday's game. Luis Enrique had rested him after the recent international break, allowing Dembélé to sit out Saturday's home game against Le Mans, and he looked razor-sharp against City.

"After the international break I went on holiday. Actually, I might ask for more holidays," Dembélé told broadcaster Canal Plus. "I really enjoy playing on Tuesday and Wednesday, especially when I come back from holiday. It's a real pleasure."

Asked if he would go on holiday again, a smiling Dembélé added: "It's possible, until March I think. It's the coach who decides."

PSG have a trip to Strasbourg in Ligue 1 on Saturday, ahead of another high-profile Champions League game at home to Lamine Yamal's free-scoring Barcelona next Tuesday.

Luis Enrique may again rest players. He also omitted left-back Nuno Mendes against Le Mans, while Dembélé sat out a game against Lille in Ligue 1 earlier this season.

Dembélé won the French league's best player award last season, despite starting only nine games in PSG's title-winning campaign. The decision to award him the trophy over other players who played significantly more games led to criticism.

City coach Enzo Maresca said PSG enjoy a luxury his team and other Premier League sides don't have, being able to rotate players against modest Ligue 1 sides.

"They can manage players when they play games before the Champions League," he said. "For us, it's a bit different, especially when you go [to] Anfield."

City played Premier League rival Liverpool in a heated atmosphere on Sunday, giving Maresca's side one day less to prepare for the PSG game.

Last season, the French league accepted PSG's request to postpone their game against title rival Lens to allow better preparation for a Champions League quarterfinal against Liverpool -- a decision perceived by some observers as preferential treatment.

PSG went on to win the trophy for a second straight year, beating Arsenal on penalties in the final.

Dembélé has scored three Champions League goals, but has not yet found the net in four Ligue 1 matches this season. PSG are in sixth place after six rounds and some performances have fallen below expectations.

"We couldn't care less that people doubted us. We're in October, it's only the second game of the Champions League," he said. "We just need to stay on track during the first half of the season and prepare for the second."

However, he acknowledged PSG's concentration dropped off against City.

"We eased up a bit in the second half," Dembélé said. "When you do that against players like that, you pay for it."
